clips.caption:
Nobody starts out this way.

Strip away the diagnosis and the real definition is simpler than you'd think: a person who feels totally and completely empty inside, no matter what they build or achieve. So they go looking outside themselves for something to fill it — your attention, your approval, your energy, anything that makes them feel like they exist at all.

Most people don't live like this. Most people carry some sense of groundedness, of knowing who they are without anyone else in the room.

This isn't a personality flaw. It's biology.

Every time a child is thrown into fight or flight — and it happens on a loop, not once — cortisol floods the brain. Do that long enough and the limbic system, the emotional core, stops developing normally. It stays hypersensitive for life.

So the adult version of that brain reads an eye roll, a tone of voice, as a threat to survival. The logical part shuts off completely, and what's left is raw, unfiltered emotion — what shows up on the outside as narcissistic rage.
